title: Renewal (V)
hookLine: old clocks needed winding daily and a cleaning once a year; Francis de Sales says a good heart does too
tomorrow: a young nun writes her whole life story. who asked her to?

cards: A phone updates itself overnight while you sleep. Old clocks couldn't. They needed a key every day, and still, now and then, someone had to open the case, clean the gears and set them right, or they'd drift.
That's Francis de Sales's answer to yesterday's question. A good heart drifts too, he says. Daily prayer keeps it wound.
Once a year, it needs a thorough cleaning.

teach.b: Start with the drift. Our good resolutions slip over time, Francis says. Not because they were false, but because people are like that.
So he builds renewal into the plan. Next, the cleaning.
Look back over the resolutions made at the start, and examine the soul honestly: how it stands toward God, toward itself, toward its neighbors. No anxiety, after yesterday. Just a clear look.
Then, the reasons. He sets out things to stir the heart again: God's goodness, the dignity of the soul, the example of the saints, the love Christ showed.
Not to scold, but to remind a person why they began. Last, the renewal itself.
Take up the resolutions again, freely and fresh, and set them before God.
Here's one to tell a friend tonight: this book about holiness doesn't end on a grand finale. It ends on a maintenance plan.
And with that, the book Francis wrote to Philothea closes: wound daily, cleaned once a year, still keeping time.

how: Some Catholics make a yearly retreat, a few quiet days of prayer, and use it to look back over their lives and renew their resolutions; the Church also renews baptismal promises together at Easter.

o: making a brand-new list of rules each day
taking up good resolutions again, fresh
starting your whole faith over from nothing

s: renewal means starting your faith over from scratch
it means taking up the same good resolutions again, fresh, after an honest look.
Francis says resolutions drift because they were false to begin with
they slip because people are like that, so he builds renewal into the plan.
the last part of the Introduction is about renewing resolutions
a clock wound daily still needs a yearly cleaning.

games.q: your youth group plans a weekend retreat, and someone says skip the looking back, just set new goals. what does Francis put first?
o: an honest look at how you stand toward God, yourself and others.
a fresh list of goals bigger than last year's.
a detailed list of every failure from the year.
games.why: his renewal starts with a clear look back, without anxiety, then reasons to stir the heart, then the old resolutions taken up again.

practice: Find a pen and paper. If a clock or a watch ticks nearby, listen to a few beats first. Then write one resolution for this year in a single short sentence, by hand, plain enough to keep.
If you pray, you can offer it to God and ask for help to keep it.

wordCard.voice: Renewal. Taking up your good resolutions again, fresh, after an honest look back.

orig.note: Latin, from the Vulgate of Ephesians 4:23: be renewed, in the spirit of your mind.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: renew yearly, because a clock that gets cleaned keeps time. Tomorrow, a new book opens.
